# Sirach Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** A wise judge shapes his people. Good leadership comes from understanding.

**2** The people are like their ruler. A city takes the character of whoever leads it.

**3** An undisciplined king destroys his people. A city is built up by the wisdom of its leaders.

**4** Authority over the earth belongs to God — and at exactly the right time, he places exactly the right person in charge.

**5** Human success is entirely in God's hands. He is the one who gives dignity to those who make the laws.

**6** Don't hold grudges against your neighbor for wrongs they've done you. Don't act with arrogance in anything.

**7** Arrogance is repulsive to God and to other people alike. And injustice is an offense to both.

**8** Power shifts from nation to nation because of violence, pride, and the grasping for wealth.

**9** What does a lump of clay have to be proud of? Even while you're alive, your body is already decomposing.

**10** A long illness makes a fool of even the best physician. A king is alive today — dead tomorrow.

**11** When you die, you become food for worms and maggots.

**12** Where does human pride begin? It begins when a person abandons God — when the heart turns away from its Maker.

**13** Pride is sin's starting point. People who cling to it produce one outrage after another. That is why God sends extraordinary disasters on them and overturns everything they built.

**14** God has pulled rulers off their thrones and put the humble in their seats.

**15** God has uprooted proud nations and planted the lowly in their place.

**16** God has devastated the lands of the nations and leveled them down to the foundations.

**17** He has swept some of them off the earth completely and wiped out all memory of them.

**18** Arrogance was not made for human beings. Violent anger was not made for those born of woman.

**19** What kind of person deserves honor? The one who fears the Lord. What kind of person deserves contempt? The one who breaks his commandments.

**20** Among your own community, a leader is worthy of honor. But those who fear the Lord — they are worthy of honor in God's eyes.

**21** The fear of the Lord is where his acceptance of us begins. Stubbornness and pride are where his rejection begins.

**22** Rich, famous, or poor — it doesn't matter. True glory is the fear of the Lord.

**23** It makes no sense to look down on a poor person who has wisdom, or to honor a person who is a sinner.

**24** The great man, the judge, the ruler — all worthy of respect. But none of them surpasses the one who fears the Lord.

**25** Free citizens may end up serving a wise slave. An intelligent person accepts that without complaint.

**26** Don't show off your cleverness at work. Don't choose the wrong moment to prove how smart you are.

**27** A worker who has more than enough is better off than someone who makes a big impression but can't put food on the table.

**28** My child, maintain your dignity — with humility. Value yourself for exactly what you are worth.

**29** Can anyone clear a person who ruins themselves? Can anyone honor a person who dishonors their own life?

**30** The poor person earns honor through knowledge. The rich person earns honor through wealth.

**31** If someone is honored even in poverty, imagine how much more when they have wealth! And if someone is scorned even when rich, imagine how much worse when they are poor!
